node.title: Microbes in Human Welfare: Microbes in household products; Microbes in industrial

questions.stem: The dough used for making bread rises because of carbon dioxide released by
questions.explanation: Baker's yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, ferments the sugars in the dough and releases carbon dioxide. The gas gets trapped in the sticky dough, which makes it puff up and rise. Hence yeast is used in baking bread.

optionRationale.1: Lactobacillus converts milk into curd and does not leaven bread dough.
optionRationale.3: Propionibacterium makes the holes in Swiss cheese.

questions.objective: Name the microbe used in bread making

questions.stem: Alexander Fleming first obtained the antibiotic penicillin from the mould
questions.explanation: Fleming noticed that bacterial colonies did not grow around a mould contaminant, and this mould was Penicillium notatum. Ernest Chain and Howard Florey later established its full potential as an effective antibiotic.

optionRationale.1: Aspergillus niger is used for citric acid production.

questions.stem: Toddy, a traditional drink of some parts of southern India, is made by fermenting the sap of
questions.explanation: Toddy is prepared by the natural fermentation of the sap collected from palms. Wine is made from grape juice and beer from malted barley, which are other well known traditional fermented beverages.

optionRationale.1: Grape juice is fermented to make wine.
optionRationale.2: Malted barley is used for making beer.
optionRationale.3: Distilled products such as rum come from sugarcane molasses and are not toddy.

questions.objective: State the raw material of toddy

questions.stem: Statins, used to lower blood cholesterol, are obtained from the yeast
questions.explanation: Statins are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus. They act as competitive inhibitors of the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol, and so lower the cholesterol level in blood.

optionRationale.2: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the yeast of bread and beer.
optionRationale.4: Streptococcus is a bacterium that gives streptokinase.

questions.stem: The fungus Glomus forms mycorrhiza on the roots of many plants. Its main benefit to the plant is that it
options: kills insect larvae feeding on the roots
absorbs phosphorus from the soil and passes it to the plant
converts soil nitrate into nitrogen gas
questions.explanation: In mycorrhizal association the fungal hyphae absorb phosphorus from the soil and supply it to the plant. Such plants also show resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and better growth.

optionRationale.1: Nodule formation and nitrogen fixation is the work of Rhizobium.
optionRationale.2: Insect control is done by biocontrol agents such as Bacillus thuringiensis.
optionRationale.4: Conversion of nitrate to nitrogen gas is denitrification and not a benefit of Glomus.

questions.stem: The main constituent of biogas produced from cattle dung is
questions.explanation: Biogas is a mixture of gases produced by methanogens such as Methanobacterium during anaerobic digestion of dung, and methane is its chief component. Carbon dioxide and hydrogen are present in smaller amounts, and the mixture burns as fuel.

optionRationale.1: Carbon monoxide is not a product of this digestion.
optionRationale.3: Ethanol is a product of yeast fermentation, not of methanogens.
optionRationale.4: Nitrogen dioxide is not a constituent of biogas.

questions.objective: Identify the main gas in biogas

questions.stem: Which pair of microbes are free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria used as biofertilisers?
questions.explanation: Azospirillum and Azotobacter live freely in the soil and fix atmospheric nitrogen, adding it to the soil. Rhizobium, in contrast, fixes nitrogen only in symbiosis with legume roots, and Glomus is a fungus.

optionRationale.1: Rhizobium is symbiotic, and Glomus is a fungus that helps in phosphorus uptake.
optionRationale.2: Both Trichoderma and Glomus are fungi and neither is a nitrogen fixer.
optionRationale.3: Bacillus thuringiensis is a biocontrol agent and Rhizobium is symbiotic.

questions.stem: A plant operator by mistake adds a strong dose of antibiotics to the aeration tank of a sewage treatment plant. The most likely result is that
options: the BOD falls faster as fewer microbes compete for oxygen
large amounts of methane are produced in the aeration tank
the aerobic bacteria that form flocs are killed, so organic matter is not oxidised and the BOD of the effluent remains high
the flocs grow larger and the effluent becomes clearer
questions.explanation: Secondary treatment depends on the aerobic bacteria that grow as flocs and oxidise organic matter. Antibiotics would kill them, so the organic load would not be consumed and the BOD would stay high instead of falling.

optionRationale.1: Fewer microbes means less consumption of organic matter, so the BOD would rise, not fall.
optionRationale.2: Methane forms under anaerobic conditions in the sludge digester, not in the aerated tank.
optionRationale.4: Without living bacteria the flocs would not form or grow.

questions.objective: Predict the effect of killing flocs on BOD

questions.stem:
Arrange the stages of sewage treatment in the correct order.
(i) Settling of flocs as activated sludge
(ii) Removal of grit by sedimentation
(iii) Growth of aerobic microbes as flocs in the aeration tank
(iv) Release of the effluent into a natural water body
questions.explanation: Primary treatment first removes grit by sedimentation. The effluent then enters the aeration tank for secondary treatment, where flocs grow. The flocs settle as activated sludge, and the cleared effluent finally goes into a river or other water body.

optionRationale.1: Flocs cannot form before the physical removal of grit and debris.
optionRationale.3: Flocs must grow before they can settle as sludge.
optionRationale.4: Activated sludge cannot form before primary treatment and aeration.

questions.objective: Sequence the stages of sewage treatment

questions.stem: Match the biofertiliser in List-I with its description in List-II.
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes. Azotobacter fixes nitrogen as a free-living soil bacterium. Glomus is the mycorrhizal fungus that helps phosphorus uptake, and Anabaena is an autotrophic cyanobacterium that fixes nitrogen in paddy fields.

optionRationale.2: This pairs 'Rhizobium' with 'Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium of the soil', which describes 'Azotobacter'.
optionRationale.3: This pairs 'Glomus' with 'Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium of paddy fields', which describes 'Anabaena'.
optionRationale.4: This pairs 'Rhizobium' with 'Fungus forming mycorrhiza that helps in phosphorus absorption', which describes 'Glomus'.

right: I. Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium of paddy fields
II. Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium of the soil
III. Symbiotic bacterium in root nodules of legumes
IV. Fungus forming mycorrhiza that helps in phosphorus absorption

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Bottled fruit juices are clearer than juices squeezed directly from the fruit.
Reason (R): Pectinases and proteases are used to break down pectin and proteins that make the juice turbid.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Freshly squeezed juice is cloudy because of pectin and protein. Pectinases and proteases break these down, which clarifies the bottled juice. So both statements are true and R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is the reason for A, so it is an explanation.
optionRationale.4: A is true and R is true.

questions.objective: Explain the use of enzymes in juice clarification

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Antibiotics are effective in treating the common cold.
Reason (R): Antibiotics are chemicals produced by some microbes that can kill or retard the growth of other, disease-causing microbes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The common cold is caused by viruses and antibiotics act against bacteria, so A is false. R correctly defines antibiotics as chemicals produced by microbes that kill or retard other microbes. So A is false and R is true.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.2: A is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.stem: Match the item in List-I with its description in List-II.
questions.explanation: Primary treatment is a physical process. Secondary treatment is a biological process in aeration tanks. The sediment of flocs is activated sludge, a part of which is returned to the tank as inoculum. Methanobacterium makes methane in the digester.

optionRationale.1: This pairs 'Primary treatment' with 'Biological treatment of the effluent in aeration tanks', which describes 'Secondary treatment'.
optionRationale.2: This pairs 'Activated sludge' with 'Methanogen that produces biogas', which describes 'Methanobacterium'.
optionRationale.3: This pairs 'Primary treatment' with 'Sediment of flocs, part of which is used as inoculum', which describes 'Activated sludge'.

right: I. Physical removal of floating debris and grit
III. Sediment of flocs, part of which is used as inoculum
IV. Biological treatment of the effluent in aeration tanks

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about penicillin.
A. Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming while working on Staphylococcus.
B. Its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey.
C. Penicillin was the first antibiotic to be discovered and is obtained from a bacterium.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Fleming observed the effect of a mould on Staphylococcus, and Chain and Florey later developed it into a useful antibiotic. Penicillin is obtained from the mould Penicillium, a fungus, not from a bacterium, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.2: C is wrong, since penicillin comes from a fungus.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.4: C is wrong, so not all three are correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on the discovery of penicillin

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about biofertilisers.
A. Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil.
B. The main sources of biofertilisers are bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria.
C. Cyanobacteria also add organic matter to the soil and increase its fertility.
D. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in association with the roots of cereals such as wheat.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Biofertilisers are living organisms such as bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria that enrich the soil, and cyanobacteria also add organic matter. Rhizobium forms nodules with legumes, not cereals, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: C is also correct, so this misses it.
optionRationale.2: D is wrong, since Rhizobium is associated with legumes.
optionRationale.4: A is correct and D is wrong.
